standard_prerequisites.name: Cut rank of a deduction
standard_prerequisites.statement: The cut rank of a natural deduction term measures the size of its largest redex, computed from the lengths of the formulas at the elimination-introduction pairs; the cut rank of a variable is the length of its type.
standard_prerequisites.use: The lemma compares the cut rank of the substituted deduction with that of M and with the length of A (620-637).

standard_prerequisites.name: Substitution of deductions
standard_prerequisites.statement: Substituting a deduction N of A for the assumption variable x in M replaces every free occurrence of x in M by N.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof inspects how redexes can be created by this substitution, case by case (638-663).

standard_prerequisites.name: Redex in natural deduction terms
standard_prerequisites.statement: A redex is an elimination immediately applied to an introduction of the matching connective, such as a conjunction elimination acting on a conjunction introduction.
standard_prerequisites.use: The four enumerated cases classify exactly which introduction inside the substituted term meets which elimination (622-631).

core_obligations: Case of a variable different from x: the substitution changes nothing, so no redex arises (640-642).
Case of a conjunction introduction, an abstraction, or a disjunction introduction at the top of M: substitution preserves that form, and the form carries no redex at its root (644-646).

Case of a conjunction elimination on P: if P is itself a conjunction introduction, the substituted deduction is a redex of the same shape with equal cut rank; if P is the variable x, the substituted deduction is the elimination acting on N, which must be a conjunction introduction, and its cut rank equals the cut rank of x, that is the length of A (648-661).
The disjunction-elimination and application cases are the mirror images of the displayed conjunction case, with the same conclusion about where the redex arises and what the cut rank is (662-663).

proof_roadmap.step: Work the conjunction-elimination cases with the cut-rank computations.
Cover the mirror cases by the declared similar argument.

difficulty_reason: The counted lemma is the author lemma at source lines 620-637: when substituting a deduction N of A for x in M produces a redex and M is not the variable x, the redex arises in one of four enumerated ways, and the cut rank of the substituted deduction is either the cut rank of M or the length of A. The author proof (638-663) runs induction on M, working the variable case, the redex-preserving cases and the conjunction-elimination cases in full detail with the displayed computations of the substituted deductions and their cut ranks, and finally covers the remaining elimination and application cases by the explicitly declared mirror argument. The case bookkeeping against the four-clause statement is real proof-theoretic work.
